title: Learning from Examples
outcome: By the end, I can compare candidate models, resolve a tie explicitly and separate fit from prediction.
scenario: A fictional classifier learns whether measured sticks are short or long.
given: Training lengths 2,4,8,10 cm have labels short,short,long,long.
Candidate boundaries: long at least 5 or at least 7. Lowest errors wins; tie chooses smaller boundary.

steps.label: Training rows
steps.detail: 2 and 4 are short; 8 and 10 are long.

steps.label: Candidate checks
steps.detail: Boundaries 5 and 7 both predict S,S,L,L: zero errors each.

steps.label: Tie policy
steps.detail: Choose boundary 5 because the declared tie rule prefers the smaller value.

steps.label: New prediction
steps.detail: Length 6 is predicted long by the selected rule.

explanation: There is no training stick between 4 and 8 to distinguish these candidates. The tie policy chooses one consistently; it is not additional evidence that its prediction at 6 is true. Label-free prediction applies the selected boundary, while evaluation would require an appropriate new reference label.

counterfactual.change: Reverse the tie policy to prefer the larger boundary.
counterfactual.prediction: Boundary 7 is selected and predicts short at 6.
counterfactual.reason: The training fit is unchanged; only the explicit choice between tied candidates changes.

student_task: Which new measured length would reveal disagreement between the candidates?
teacher_answer: Length 6 does: boundary 5 predicts long and boundary 7 predicts short. A checked label would then provide new evidence.
project_evidence: Save candidate definitions, training errors and tie policy with any sorter model version.
limits: Zero training errors for both rules cannot determine the correct label of every unobserved stick.
review_note: New fictional worked case reviewed against the weekly topic and reserved independent assessment. Keep that assessment separate; this picture is supported practice.

mini_visual.title: Same training errors, different new prediction
